s50m:S1Q04F.q: How would you reduce the sorting cost for millions of customers while preserving the tie rule?
s50m:S1Q04F.label: gemini-3.1-flash-lite_fturn-s50m-A
s50m:S1Q04F.spoken: For millions of records, a full sort is inefficient. I’d use a min-heap of size K to track the top candidates, which reduces the complexity to O(N log K). To preserve the tie-breaking rule, I’d store tuples of (score, index) in the heap, ensuring the comparison logic explicitly checks the secondary index if scores are equal. If I need even faster performance, I’d use a Quickselect algorithm to partition the data in O(N) average time, avoiding a full sort entirely.

s50m:S1Q06F.q: How would you index those tables, and what changes if historical records can be corrected after ingestion?
s50m:S1Q06F.label: gemini-3.1-flash-lite_fturn-s50m-A
s50m:S1Q06F.spoken: I’d use a composite B-tree index on customer_id and event_timestamp to optimize time-series lookups, and partition by time to keep performance stable. For corrections, I avoid destructive updates by using a "valid_from" and "valid_to" versioning pattern. This creates an audit trail, letting me reconstruct the data state at any point in time, which is crucial for preventing training-serving skew.

s50m:S2Q05F.q: Construct an example where that greedy policy gives poor coverage, and tell me how you would incorporate redundancy or multi hop dependence
s50m:S2Q05F.label: gemini-3.1-flash-lite_fturn-s50m-A
s50m:S2Q05F.spoken: A greedy relevance-first policy fails when the top-k chunks are redundant, like retrieving five paragraphs that all define the same term but miss the actual answer. I’d fix this by implementing Maximal Marginal Relevance, which penalizes chunks similar to those already selected, forcing the system to pick novel information. For multi-hop dependencies, I use agentic decomposition to break the query into sub-questions, ensuring each retrieval step is contextually grounded in the previous one.

s50m:S2Q08F.q: How do you prove the replacement index is sufficiently complete and current before you send production traffic to it?
s50m:S2Q08F.label: gemini-3.1-flash-lite_fturn-s50m-A
s50m:S2Q08F.spoken: I run the new index in shadow mode, mirroring production traffic to both indexes. I compare retrieval quality using a golden set of queries, measuring MRR and hit rate against the baseline. For completeness, I run automated checksums on the ingestion pipeline and use an LLM-as-judge to verify the retrieved context remains relevant before the final cutover.
